109 segregant strains from a cross between the parental strains were grown in two conditions

Two parental strains (BY and RM, see Materials and Methods ) and 109 segregant strains from a cross between the parental strains were grown in two conditions—glucose and ethanol as carbon sources—and expression profiled using microarrays.
3,997 and 3,489 linkages were observed in glucose and ethanol
We performed linkage analysis on the transcript levels within each condition, and 3,997 and 3,489 linkages were observed in glucose and ethanol, respectively ( Figure S1 and Table S4 ).
subjected to linkage analysis with 2,894 markers

The difference between conditions was calculated for each segregant for 4,482 transcripts with high-quality data (see Materials and Methods ), and subjected to linkage analysis with 2,894 markers spaced throughout the genome.
There were 1,382 transcripts that showed gene–environment interaction with at least one locus

There were 1,382 transcripts that showed gene–environment interaction with at least one locus (total of 1,555 linkages) at a genome-wide 5% false discovery rate (FDR), as determined by permutation (see Figure 3 for an example).
172/1,555 (11%) of all gxe QTL being local
gxe QTL were less likely to be local, with 172/1,555 (11%) of all gxe QTL being local, as compared to linkages within either condition, where 22%–25% of all linkages were local ( Table 1 ).
81% (1,126/1,383) of distant gxe QTL occurring in 31/563 bins
The majority of distant linkages fell into bins with a significant excess of linkages, with 81% (1,126/1,383) of distant gxe QTL occurring in 31/563 bins, or 5.5% of the genome.
Significant bins that were located immediately next to each other were merged into a single peak to form 13, 13, and 15 peaks

Significant bins that were located immediately next to each other were merged into a single peak to form 13, 13, and 15 peaks for glucose, ethanol, and gxe QTL, respectively ( Figure 4 and Table S1 ).
Some of these regions coincided with loci that have been characterized at the gene level
Some of these regions coincided with loci that have been characterized at the gene level, including AMN1 [ 35 ], GPA1 [ 35 ], MAT [ 19 ], HAP1 [ 9 ], and IRA2 (this paper).
Thirteen peaks were found in each condition, but only seven were found in both.
Thirteen peaks were found in each condition, but only seven were found in both.
In glucose, 49 transcripts show distant linkage here, whereas in ethanol, there are no distant linkages
In glucose, 49 transcripts show distant linkage here, whereas in ethanol, there are no distant linkages, suggesting that the polymorphism in GPA1 does not influence these transcripts in ethanol.
Allele replacements of DIG1 in both backgrounds show that variants in DIG1 make a major contribution
Allele replacements of DIG1 in both backgrounds show that variants in DIG1 make a major contribution to the effects at this locus ( Figure S3 ).
A total of 386 transcripts show distant linkage to this locus in ethanol
A total of 386 transcripts show distant linkage to this locus in ethanol, whereas in glucose, only ten show distant linkage.
only 965/1,555 (62%) gxe QTL also reached genome-wide significance levels

Comparisons of gxe QTL with linkage results for transcript levels in glucose or ethanol showed that only 965/1,555 (62%) gxe QTL also reached genome-wide significance levels in at least one condition (see Figure S2 B for full Venn diagram).
All 1,555 gxe QTL showed an effect in at least one condition

All 1,555 gxe QTL showed an effect in at least one condition, with 265/1,555 (17%) showing an effect only in glucose, 327/1,555 (21%) showing an effect only in ethanol, and 963/1,555 (62%) showing an effect in both conditions.
546/1,383 (40%) of distant linkages were significant in only one condition

Distant linkages were significantly more likely to be condition specific than local linkages, as 546/1,383 (40%) of distant linkages were significant in only one condition, as compared to 46/172 (27%) of local linkages ( Table 2 and see Figure 5 for a schematic).
A total of 372 transcripts link here distantly
A total of 372 transcripts link here distantly, and many are generally involved in energy metabolism and growth ( Figure 7 A).

Many transcripts link to this region in glucose and ethanol (1,159 and 410, respectively)

Many transcripts link to this region in glucose and ethanol (1,159 and 410, respectively), and IRA2 polymorphisms also contribute to the variation in transcript levels within these conditions ( Figure S4 ).
Three phenotypes were used in linkage analysis
Three phenotypes were used in linkage analysis: expression in glucose, expression in ethanol, and the difference in expression between glucose and ethanol (ethanol minus glucose for each segregant).
Our final set of markers consisted of 2,894 markers
Our final set of markers consisted of 2,894 markers with an average spacing of 4 kb or 1.9 cM.
LOD scores of 3.25, 3.3, and 3.7 corresponded to FDRs of 4.9%, 4.9%, and 4.8%
LOD scores of 3.25, 3.3, and 3.7 corresponded to FDRs of 4.9%, 4.9%, and 4.8% for glucose, ethanol, and the difference between condition phenotypes, respectively.
We also calculated confidence intervals as LOD support regions
We also calculated confidence intervals as LOD support regions that extend outward from the peak marker until the LOD score decreases by 1.5 LOD units [ 52 ].
A linkage was classified as a local linkage if the confidence interval of the linkage overlapped
A linkage was classified as a local linkage if the confidence interval of the linkage overlapped with the region containing the open reading frame of the gene of interest (ORF region).
The two markers flanking the region from 500 bp upstream of the start of the ORF
The two markers flanking the region from 500 bp upstream of the start of the ORF to 500 bp downstream of the stop of the ORF, as defined by the Saccharomyces Genome Database, defined the ORF region.

Of the 4,342 transcripts with high-quality data, 2,037 (47%)

Of the 4,342 transcripts with high-quality data, 2,037 (47%), 2,996 (69%), and 3,448 (79%) showed significant effects due to strain–condition interaction, strain, and condition, respectively (see Figure 1 B and 1 C for strong examples and Table S3 for a full list).
